name: 264. Provider key server-secret references on a whitelisted management route (key-secret-refs-e2e)
description: Opt-in profile regression for TXE-4989. Run with provider_config/whitelisted-provider-keys/config.json (setup_token set, no admin, client.whitelisted_routes ["/api/providers/*"]) on an isolated fresh instance, INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1, PARALLEL=0 and FEATURE=key-secret-refs-e2e; the harness's setup token must be the profile's (BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN, default bifrost-e2e-setup-token). With dashboard auth off, an operator-whitelisted /api route passes the OSS setup lock and is admitted by the fail-open bypass without any credential, which is how a caller with no credential reaches the provider-key handlers over HTTP in OSS (the other reachable bypasses are a gateway with no config store and enterprise builds with auth off). Before the fix such a caller could create or repoint a key whose value is an env./vault. reference, and the gateway resolved the server secret and sent it to the provider. Case 1 proves the lock is active for routes that are not whitelisted; case 2 creates a custom provider with an extra header referencing an env. variable as the setup-token admin (POST /api/providers is not under the whitelisted prefix; base_url 127.0.0.1:9, where nothing listens, so nothing leaves the host). Cases 3-5 cover the provider extra-header rule (TXE-5411) on this reachable path, correcting folder 263's claim that it had none in OSS: with no credential, resending the unchanged reference succeeds, repointing it gets the provider handler's 403, and the stored reference is unchanged. Cases 6-12 (TXE-5528 inserts the two case-variant cases after the value repoint: a case-variant name reaches the same refusal, and an edit under one applies) cover keys. Case 6 creates a key with an env. reference with no credential and expects the key handler's 403, not the lock's 401 (red before the fix); case 7 shows nothing was stored (red before the fix); case 8 creates a literal key, which stays allowed; case 9 repoints its value to an env. reference and expects the 403 (red before the fix); case 10 shows an edit that leaves the value alone still succeeds; case 11 shows the literal survived (red before the fix); the last case deletes the provider. The key rows reference HOME, a non-secret variable every gateway process has, so before the fix the reference resolves and the key is stored (an unset variable would be refused for an empty value and show nothing); the header variables are not set. No secret exists to leak in either build. The openai keyword is only a harness filter label; no provider calls are made. Cookies and redirect following are disabled. Every unexpected status fails. Run the whole folder in order.
